items.title: Seven members of Iran's women's football team have sought asylum, ABC understands
items.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke, who was at the airport, said border force officials made multiple representations to all of the team before departing Sydney.

items.title: Live: Iran 'not seeking ceasefire' as US and Israel continue to pummel Tehran
items.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says the US is hitting Iran with the "most intense" day of strikes since the war began. Follow live.

items.title: Asian hubs boom as Australians avoid Middle East airspace
items.description: Flights in limbo, a region at war, and thousands of dollars lost with no end in sight — Australian travellers are going to extreme lengths to keep their hopes of a European holiday alive despite the dire circumstances.

items.title: Iran hit with 'most intense' day of strikes, Hegseth says
items.description: The US has been pounding Iran with its "most intense" day of strikes since the war began, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says.

items.title: Head in the sand? Why our markets keep pushing higher
items.description: "Up the stairs and down the elevator" has been the rule of thumb for decades in financial markets — but apparently it's not the case any longer.

items.title: 'I'm buggered': A teary Littleproud says it's time for a new Nationals leader
items.description: The Queenslander cried as he spoke to reporters, saying it had been a "pretty rough" time since the May election.

items.title: Government moves to temporarily ban 'certain cohorts' from Australia
items.description: Visitors from some countries could be temporarily blocked from Australia by a federal government concerned about a wave of people overstaying their visas due to the war in the Middle East.

items.title: 'Jackie told me she was hurt': Sandilands responds to radio drama
items.description: In his first statement since he was ordered off the air after a blow-up with co-host Jackie "O" Henderson, Sandilands calls on ARN Media, owner of KIIS FM, to "honour our agreement" and let him return to the Kyle and Jackie O Show.

items.title: Bundaberg residents told to 'leave immediately' as floodwaters rise, bridges shut
items.description: A major flood is threatening Bundaberg after days of rain spilled dams and set rivers on the rise across Queensland.

items.title: Lululemon fined $700,000 over hundreds of thousands of spam emails
items.description: The Australian Communications and Media Authority says activewear fashion brand Lululemon sent more than 370,000 emails containing marketing content without an unsubscribe option.

items.title: Family of 14yo says Aidan Becker 'risked his life to save our son'
items.description: The family of a 14-year-old boy allegedly attacked in Mernda last week said Aidan Becker, who was fatally stabbed trying to protect the teenager, showed "extraordinary courage and compassion in risking his life to save our son".

items.title: Consumer watchdog keeping tabs on fuel price hikes
items.description: Australia's consumer watchdog is watching fuel companies as prices surge past $2.50 a litre, driven by a Middle East war that has pushed global oil to nearly $US120 a barrel.

items.title: Data reveals demands on NSW hospitals have surpassed COVID pandemic
items.description: The latest figures released by the Bureau of Health Information paints a picture of a health system which remains under immense pressure with record numbers also recorded in admitted patient episodes.

items.title: Digital harassment, child abuse material common federal crimes in Vic
items.description: Digital crimes involving harassment, or distributing child abuse material, are among the most common federal crimes being sentenced in Victoria, a new report shows.

items.title: Two new novels lift the curtain on what life is really like as a royal
items.description: With Queen Mary of Denmark soon to arrive in Australia and scandal engulfing the House of Windsor, royals are swamping our news cycle. So why are readers so fascinated by royal fiction?

items.title: Kurt Cobain's Smells Like Teen Spirit guitar could fetch up to $7m at auction
items.description: The iconic six-string that gave a sound to an era's angst is among a treasure trove of items set to be sold at a New York auction.

items.title: Outback police officer wrangles freshwater croc in backyard
items.description: Fitzroy Crossing police officer-in-charge Mark Howes says no-one else was available to help remove a freshwater crocodile from a local backyard, "so I thought I'd have a crack".

items.title: Pilbara artist's work to be shown in Sydney after 5,000km road trip
items.description: From the Pilbara to Penrith, an Indigenous WA community has taken its prized cultural and artistic possessions across the country for the Biennale of Sydney.

items.title: Star Hawk regrets 'foolish mistake' that landed him in US jail
items.description: Dylan Moore opens up on an off-season incident involving a scissor-lift that cost him his Hawthorn vice-captaincy.

items.title: Lions' defensive stocks cop major blow after unsuccessful tribunal date
items.description: Brisbane must tackle a red-hot Sydney side without two of its most important defenders after the AFL tribunal upheld bans handed to Harris Andrews and Darcy Gardiner.

items.title: Court orders Linda Reynolds and Commonwealth to enter mediation
items.description: The Federal Court orders mediation between former WA senator Linda Reynolds and the Commonwealth in her legal claim over its conduct during a financial settlement with Brittany Higgins.

items.title: Hobart stadium not expected to be ready for AFL Devils games until 2031
items.description: When the $1.13 billion stadium was approved last year, it was hoped the Tasmania Devils would begin playing AFL games there from 2029. The head of the corporation tasked with delivering the stadium says her expectations are set a little bit later.

items.title: Blond echidnas and other rare animals caught on remote island cameras
items.description: Wildlife cameras snap rare pictures of blond echidnas, a tiny white-footed dunnart, and threatened seabirds on a small island off Tasmania's north coast.

items.title: Driver says those killed in 'incomprehensible tragedy' are with him always
items.description: The driver who was behind the wheel of a car that ploughed into a group of people outside a central Victorian pub has detailed his sorrow over the crash.

items.title: Barry Cable abused girl from orphanage in Perth home as wife slept, court hears
items.description: Ex-Australian football Hall of Famer Barry Cable picked up a girl from an orphanage in Perth and sexually abused her multiple times in the 1960s, a court has been told.
